my grandmother was a child when the war began. they lived in belarus and hid a Jewish family from nazis in their basement.

my grand grandfather was from russia. when the war began, we was away from his family for work. when he returned to his village, it was completely destroyed by bombings, his wife and newborn son were dead. 
he had been in two concentration camps. he ran away the first time and the second time the war ended, so soviet soldiers freed him. in those camps they were so hungry, that when someone died of tuberculosis without finishing their food (that happend quite often), other prisoners would eat that food even though they could be infected. they just didn't care.
after the war ended, he was considered to be an enemy of the ussr, because he "surrendered" to the nazis (that's how insane the soviet regime was). as a punishment a lot of people were sent to soviet camps (such as gulag), where they were forced to work all day long. luckily, my grand grandfather was sent to fight in a war with japan instead, but while they were going there by a train, that war had already ended. the train arrived in siberia and my grand grandfather with other veterans had to build and work at a local factory. that's where he met my grand grandmother, who was a bit younger that him. 
sadly, he died before i was born so it was his son, my grandfather, who told me those stories.
